title: 🪟 A Windows Zero-Day Bypasses the Lock Screen — with No Fix!
body: 🪟 A Windows Zero-Day Bypasses the Lock Screen — with No Fix!

A security researcher revealed a Windows zero-day known as “FastUnlock” that bypasses the lock screen through the “Narrator” screen reader on devices protected by BitLocker, and it still has no fix and no official vulnerability number. The flaw needs physical access to the device and a Microsoft account, and it runs its commands with the privileges of a limited account, not admin privileges, and a security company confirmed the exploitation on the same day, without publishing a list of the affected versions.
Simply put: the lock screen is the first line of defense for your device; this flaw bypasses it on a locked device, but it requires the attacker to physically hold your device.
Do you always lock your device when you walk away from it?
